issues.description: Attribute type mismatch between the problem statement UML and the solution: the UML shows numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as double, while the solution defines these attributes as int. This will confuse students about whether to implement these fields as double or int and may cause mismatches when they try to implement constructors, getters/setters, or arithmetic methods that rely on the attribute types.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the types consistent. Preferably change the UML in the problem statement to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int (to match the solution and typical usage for student counts), or alternatively update the solution/template to use double and adjust method return types and tests accordingly. Ensure UML, template, and solution all use the same types.

issues.description: Internal inconsistency in the problem statement UML: the attributes numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents are declared as double, but getTotalNumberOfStudents() is specified to return an int. Using double attributes but expecting an int total is contradictory and will confuse students about expected return types and rounding/truncation behavior.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the UML internally consistent: either declare the student-count attributes as int so that getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning int is consistent, or if the attributes should be double, change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return double (and update any dependent method signatures/examples). The clearer fix is to use int for student counts and keep getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning int.
